Convert MeteoGalicia daily observations to an ldata object

Source: R/meteogal2lfdata.R
meteogal2lfdata.Rd

Create an fda.usc::ldata object: a metadata data.frame df with one row per station-year, and one fdata element per variable.

meteogal2lfdata(
  station_ids = NULL,
  vars = NULL,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  last_n_days = 30L,
  df = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  inventory = NULL,
  output_file = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  control = list(),
  quality = c(1L, 5L)
)

Arguments

station_ids

Optional character vector of station codes.

vars

NULL for all numeric measurements present, or a character vector such as c("temp_mean", "prec").

start_date, end_date

Optional initial and final date (Date or YYYY-MM-DD).

last_n_days

Number of days for the default online interval (30).

df

Optional data.frame as returned by meteogal2df().

file

Optional .csv, .rds, .rda input file(s) or directory.

inventory

Optional station metadata as a data.frame (e.g. from meteogal2inventory()) or a .csv/.rds file. It completes missing metadata (coordinates, altitude, ...). It is not downloaded automatically.

output_file

Optional .rds, .rda or .RData output path.

verbose

Print status messages.

control

List forwarded to meteogal2df() when downloading.

quality

Validation codes whose values are used (default c(1, 5)); see meteogal2df() and meteogal_qc_codes().

Value

An ldata object (fda.usc::ldata()): df and the named fdata components, all with identical row order.

Details

All curves use argvals = 1:365: February 29 is removed and day 60 is always March 1. Days without a record and values not admitted by quality are NA (never imputed). Row names (station_year) are shared by df and every fdata element.

Columns of ldata$df

  • Station: station_id, station_name, municipality, province, altitude (m), lon, lat (completed from inventory if given).

  • Curve: year, n_days (calendar dates with a record, after removing February 29, whatever the variable), first_date, last_date, and fecha: a 365-column matrix with the date of each record (NA = no record that day).

  • For each variable v: n_v_valid (days with a value used in the curve), n_v_interp (of these, interpolated by MeteoGalicia, code 5), n_v_masked (days whose value was set to NA because its code is not in quality, e.g. 0, 2 or 3), n_v_missing (365 - n_v_valid), and qc_v: a 365-column matrix with the validation code of each day (NA = no code: day absent, or data without codes).

The matrices have class mg_daymat (see mg_daymat): they print as one summary per curve and are subset with the rows, so subset(ld, ld$df$n_temp_mean_valid >= 330) keeps curves, metadata, codes and dates aligned. Use unclass(ld$df$qc_temp_mean) for the plain matrix. Source: MeteoGalicia, Xunta de Galicia.

References

MeteoGalicia daily JSON service documentation: https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_EstacionsDiarios_es.pdf.

See also

meteogal2fdata(), meteogal2inventory(), meteogal_qc_codes()

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "meteogal_small.csv", package = "meteogal2fdata")
ld <- meteogal2lfdata(file = f, vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"))
names(ld)
#> [1] "df"        "temp_mean" "prec"     
ld$df[, c("station_id", "year", "n_days", "first_date", "last_date",
          "n_temp_mean_valid", "n_temp_mean_missing")]
#>            station_id year n_days first_date  last_date n_temp_mean_valid
#> 10157_2024      10157 2024      6 2024-01-01 2024-01-06                 6
#>            n_temp_mean_missing
#> 10157_2024                 359
ld$df$qc_temp_mean   # codes per curve (NA: this extract has no codes)
#> 10157_2024 
#>     NA:365 
ld$df$fecha
#>                 10157_2024 
#> 2024-01-01..2024-01-06 (6)
